global_organization_chain: state two outputs: leaf-shape/profile relation and total leaf mass
define two reusable foundation models for crown geometry and sunlight
convert leaves and branches into computable classes, vectors, and recursive transformations
derive a directional sky field and attenuate it through the crown
hold branching profiles fixed and compare candidate leaf shapes on weighted sunlight exposure
pass local irradiance into photosynthesis and venation relations to obtain leaf-level LMA
combine weighted LMA, projected crown area, and LAI into total leaf mass
apply the chain to one Cinnamomum camphora and to a height-profile simulation grid
separate pooled from profile-specific mass-height patterns
name classification, projection, and physiology interfaces for future improvement
translate findings and model contributions into the conclusion and journal-editor memo

main_argument_chains.claim: A recursive vector representation can supply crown and leaf geometry to both downstream applications.
support_steps: classify leaves with three computable features
represent parent-child branches by local transformations
place leaves using phyllotaxis, spacing, and occurrence rules
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the same geometric state for sunlight exposure, projected crown area, and leaf-mass aggregation.

main_argument_chains.claim: Within a fixed branching profile, candidate leaf shapes can be compared by a sky-weighted exposure score.
support_steps: derive a directional brightness field from the annual sun path
attenuate radiation along crown path length
rank four leaf classes for three profiles
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Compare the finite-set winner with the observed leaf class while retaining the sample-size and candidate-set boundary.

main_argument_chains.claim: The modeled total leaf mass is a dependency chain from local irradiance to LMA and from crown footprint to total area.
support_steps: connect photosynthesis and venation traits to individual LMA
multiply projected ground area by LAI
multiply total area by weighted LMA
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Produce a species-case mass estimate whose validity depends on the physiological parameters, LMA weights, and individual-tree LAI.

main_argument_chains.claim: Tree profile conditions the simulated relationship between height and total leaf mass.
support_steps: vary height from 5 m to 10 m
repeat the analysis within each profile
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Avoid a universal pooled correlation and report only a conditional within-profile pattern.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Local coordinate diagrams sit beside the transformation matrix, making theta and phi physically interpretable.
Overhead and oblique 3D views connect sun direction to projected crown points, but leaf polygons, union area, scale, and metric region are not shown.
A compact table aligns three tree profiles, candidate scores, chosen shape, and observed shape; score uncertainty is absent.
Four small scatter plots lack fitted equations, uncertainty, residuals, readable labels, and simulated-data status.
